werk/kenny-dorham-afro-cuban.text:
Afro-Cuban is an album by the American jazz trumpeter Kenny Dorham, recorded for Blue Note. The sessions took place on 30 January and 29 March 1955. The album was released that same year in the Blue Note Modern Jazz Series, shortly before the label discontinued that format. Alfred Lion was the producer and Rudy Van Gelder the recording engineer.

The sessions featured Hank Mobley on tenor saxophone, Cecil Payne on baritone saxophone, Horace Silver on piano and Art Blakey on drums. The March session also brought in the trombonist J.J. Johnson, the bassist Oscar Pettiford, the conga player Carlos Patato Valdes and Richie Goldberg on cowbell. This gave the record its Latin American percussion. The album was later reissued with a new cover. The reviewer for Allmusic calls it a first-rate recording by an underrated trumpeter.
werk/kenny-dorham-afro-cuban.listen: Listen to Afrodisia and notice how the trumpet and the saxophones interact with the rhythm section.

werk/kenny-dorham-jazz-contemporary.text:
Jazz Contemporary is an album by the American jazz trumpeter Kenny Dorham, recorded on 11 and 12 February 1960 and released on the Time label. It is the first recording by the pianist Steve Kuhn. The other musicians are the baritone saxophonist Charles Davis, the bassist Jimmy Garrison or Butch Warren, and the drummer Buddy Enlow. The programme consists of originals by the leader, along with Monk's Mood by Thelonious Monk, In Your Own Sweet Way by Dave Brubeck and This Love of Mine, which Frank Sinatra co-wrote.

The AllMusic reviewer gave the album two and a half stars. In his view it is not truly essential, but everyone plays well. He calls it fine hard bop, the modern mainstream of the time.
werk/kenny-dorham-jazz-contemporary.listen: Listen to Monk's Mood, a composition by Thelonious Monk, and notice how the band turns it into a relaxed hard bop piece.

werk/kenny-dorham-jazz-contrasts.text:
Jazz Contrasts is an album by the American jazz trumpeter Kenny Dorham, recorded in 1957 and released by Riverside. It has six tracks and runs for about 41 minutes. It consists mainly of well-known standards, such as Falling in Love with Love, I'll Remember April, My Old Flame and But Beautiful, supplemented by La Rue and La Villa.

Besides Dorham on trumpet, Sonny Rollins plays tenor saxophone on four tracks. The others are Hank Jones on piano, Oscar Pettiford on bass and Max Roach on drums. They are joined by the harpist Betty Glamann, who is heard on three tracks and gives the record an unusual tonal colour. According to the Allmusic reviewer, the album is on the short side but contains many memorable tracks.
werk/kenny-dorham-jazz-contrasts.listen: Listen to La Rue and notice the harp of Betty Glamann: how does it sound alongside the trumpet?

werk/kenny-g-duotones.text:
Duotones was released on 29 September 1986 by Arista Records. It is the fourth studio album by the saxophonist Kenny G. He plays all the saxophones as well as keyboards, synthesizer bass, drum machine and backing vocals. On one track he plays all the instruments himself, and he also plays an EWI, an electronic wind controller that can produce violin and horn sounds. Narada Michael Walden is the executive producer, Preston Glass is the producer, and Kenny G co-produced several tracks.

The best-known track is Songbird, which reached number four on the Billboard Hot 100. The album reached number one on the Contemporary Jazz Albums chart and number six on the Billboard 200. A second version also exists, with a slightly different running order. On it, Don't Make Me Wait for Love and What Does It Take (To Win Your Love) are longer, and there is an additional track.
werk/kenny-g-duotones.listen: Listen to the saxophone melody in Songbird and notice how lyrically and calmly he plays the line above the electronic accompaniment.

werk/kenny-loggins-celebrate-me-home.text:
Celebrate Me Home is Kenny Loggins's first solo album and was released on 13 April 1977 by Columbia Records. It was his first record since the break-up of Loggins and Messina in 1976. Phil Ramone and the jazz keyboardist Bob James produced the album, and well-known session musicians such as Lee Ritenour, Steve Gadd and Eric Gale played on it.

The sound shifts from folk rock towards smoother soft rock. Two singles were released. I Believe In Love reached number 66 in the American chart and had been sung a year earlier by Barbra Streisand for the film A Star Is Born. The title song came out in late 1977 and at first failed to chart, but it became a Christmas-season fixture on the radio. The album reached number 27 and went platinum.
werk/kenny-loggins-celebrate-me-home.listen: Listen to Celebrate Me Home and notice the warm, smooth sound of the band over which Loggins's voice lies.

werk/kenny-loggins-high-adventure.text:
High Adventure is the fourth studio album by the American singer-songwriter Kenny Loggins and was released in September 1982 by Columbia Records. Bruce Botnick and Loggins produced the record. Many guests play on it, including Michael McDonald, Steve Lukather and David Sanborn. The album is best known for three singles in the American top forty: Heart to Heart, Welcome to Heartlight and Don't Fight It.

He co-wrote Don't Fight It with Steve Perry, the singer of Journey. Perry also sings on it, and the guitarist Neil Giraldo, the husband of Pat Benatar, plays on it as well. The song was nominated for a Grammy for Best Rock Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal.
werk/kenny-loggins-high-adventure.listen: Listen to Don't Fight It and notice how two singers sing the song together.

werk/kenny-loggins-keep-the-fire.text:
Keep the Fire is the third studio album by the American singer-songwriter Kenny Loggins and was released on 26 September 1979. Tom Dowd produced the record. The best-known track is the single This Is It, co-written by Michael McDonald, who also plays on it. Michael Jackson sings backing vocals on Who's Right, Who's Wrong, and Michael Brecker plays a saxophone solo on it.

Rolling Stone called the album the new sound of Southern California: polished, jazzy pop rock from an expanded band, in which guitar and keyboards are equally important. The magazine also spoke of a romantic atmosphere around a voice that would suit a matinee idol. A Canadian newspaper felt that he occasionally slipped back into the cheerful rock sound of Loggins and Messina.
werk/kenny-loggins-keep-the-fire.listen: Listen to This Is It and notice the contribution of Michael McDonald, who also plays on it.

werk/kenny-loggins-nightwatch.text:
Nightwatch is the second studio album by Kenny Loggins and was released in 1978. It is his highest-charting album in the United States: it reached number 7 on the Billboard 200. Most of the musicians on the album formed his band from 1977 to 1980.

The first single, Whenever I Call You Friend, is a duet with Stevie Nicks of Fleetwood Mac, written with Melissa Manchester. The song reached number 5 on the Billboard Hot 100. Easy Driver was the second and last single and reached number 60 in early 1979. Nightwatch also contains the first released version of What a Fool Believes, which Loggins wrote together with Michael McDonald of the Doobie Brothers.
werk/kenny-loggins-nightwatch.listen: Listen to Whenever I Call You Friend and notice how the voices of Loggins and Stevie Nicks complement each other.

werk/king-crimson-in-the-court-of-the-cr.text:
King Crimson first played live in April 1969 and in July supported the Rolling Stones in Hyde Park. The first sessions with the producer Tony Clarke produced no result, after which the band produced the album themselves at Wessex Sound Studios in London. Ian McDonald layered Mellotron and wind instruments on top of one another for hours, creating a rich, orchestral sound. In Epitaph, he had two Mellotron parts move against each other in volume during the mixing.

The album is often regarded as the first true progressive rock album. It combines rock with jazz, classical and symphonic music, with lyrics about war, alienation and corrupt authority. 21st Century Schizoid Man was compared to heavy metal, while I Talk to the Wind is gentler and was meant to show that side of the band. It reached number five in Britain and became the group's most successful album.
werk/king-crimson-in-the-court-of-the-cr.listen: Listen in Epitaph to the layers of Mellotron moving beneath the vocals. Notice how this keeps the chords from sounding flat.

werk/king-crimson-in-the-wake-of-poseido.text:
King Crimson's second album was released in May 1970, at a moment when the group was falling apart. Ian McDonald and Michael Giles had left after the first American tour, and Greg Lake was about to join forces with Keith Emerson. Robert Fripp took over part of the keyboards. Lake nevertheless sang on almost all of the songs, the Giles brothers returned temporarily and the jazz pianist Keith Tippett took part.

The album follows the template of In the Court of the Crimson King closely. It opens with an a cappella piece, Peace, which returns twice later on. Pictures of a City has jazz influences, and the longest track, The Devils Triangle, is a dark instrumental piece based on Mars by Gustav Holst. Critics praised the performance and production, although later listeners found it too close a copy of the first record. In England the album reached number 4.
werk/king-crimson-in-the-wake-of-poseido.listen: Listen to The Devils Triangle and follow how the piece grows steadily heavier and messier until it ends in near chaos.

werk/king-crimson-islands.text:
Islands was released on 3 December 1971 and is King Crimson's fourth studio album. The line-up consisted of Robert Fripp, Peter Sinfield, Mel Collins, Boz Burrell and Ian Wallace, and stayed together for this one album only. Afterwards Fripp dismissed Sinfield from the band. As on Lizard, the album before it, jazz improvisation plays a part. Sinfield was looking for a softer, more sensual sound, like Miles Davis with vocals.

The Letters builds on an old song by Giles, Giles and Fripp. Ladies of the Road is about groupies, a lyric that Sinfield himself later called one of the most sexist lyrics of all time. Reactions were mixed. AllMusic called it the weakest studio record of the group's first period. Others praised Sailor's Tale as a masterly instrumental piece.
werk/king-crimson-islands.listen: Listen to Formentera Lady. Notice the calm, flowing build-up, in which the piece slowly changes mood.

werk/king-crimson-larks-tongues-in-aspic.text:
After the end of the Islands tour, Robert Fripp took leave of the other band members and put together an entirely new line-up. The bassist and singer John Wetton, the violinist and keyboardist David Cross, the drummer Bill Bruford and the percussionist Jamie Muir formed, together with him, the fifth King Crimson, which released the album on Island Records in 1973. Fripp now wrote harder music, inspired by Béla Bartók, Igor Stravinsky, Jimi Hendrix and free improvisation.

The violin took the place of the wind instruments, and Muir built around himself a row of found objects, bells, chains and small drums. He left the group shortly after the recording sessions, so this is the only album by this line-up. Easy Money came together bit by bit: Fripp wrote the verses, and Wetton added the chorus later. The instrumental pieces sometimes sound like jazz fusion, sometimes almost like heavy metal. The reception was mixed, but later one writer called it the most important progressive rock record of 1973.
werk/king-crimson-larks-tongues-in-aspic.listen: Listen in Larks' Tongues In Aspic, Pt. 1 (2023 Elemental Mix) to the unusual sounds of the percussion and the violin, and notice how softness and intensity alternate.

werk/king-crimson-lizard.text:
Lizard was released on 11 December 1970. The record was written and produced by the guitarist Robert Fripp and the lyricist Peter Sinfield, the two remaining founders of King Crimson. The new singer and bassist Gordon Haskell, the drummer Andy McCulloch and the saxophonist Mel Collins played on it, joined by guests such as the pianist Keith Tippett, Jon Anderson of Yes on vocals, and wind players. This line-up never played live.

Haskell and McCulloch found the recording process an unpleasant experience and left the group shortly after the record. Many wind players take part, and the longest piece, the title suite Lizard, is a suite in several parts. The cover, with medieval miniatures, was made by Gini Barris, after Sinfield's lyrics. Songs such as Cirkus and Lady of the Dancing Water only found a place in the live repertoire later.
werk/king-crimson-lizard.listen: Listen to Lizard: Prince Rupert Awakes and notice how, besides the band, wind instruments and piano also play a major role.

werk/king-crimson-starless-and-bible-bla.text:
After Larks' Tongues in Aspic, the percussionist Jamie Muir left King Crimson. The band carried on as a quartet and struggled with a lack of new material. The solution was to improvise. Much of Starless and Bible Black was recorded live and stitched onto studio work. Only The Great Deceiver and Lament were made entirely in the studio. Trio, the title piece and Fracture come from the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam, and We'll Let You Know was improvised in Glasgow. The album was released in March 1974 and is the last with the violinist David Cross as a member.

During Trio, Bill Bruford let his sticks rest crossed on his chest and decided not to play. The others considered that a crucial choice, and he received a writing credit. Rolling Stone compared the record in power to In the Court of the Crimson King.
werk/king-crimson-starless-and-bible-bla.listen: Listen to Trio. Notice what cannot be heard: the drummer plays no drums here.

werk/king-curtis-soul-meeting.text:
Soul Meeting is the sixth album by the saxophonist King Curtis and was released in 1960 by Prestige. He plays tenor saxophone, surrounded by a remarkable company: Nat Adderley on trumpet and cornet, Wynton Kelly on piano, Sam Jones and Paul Chambers on bass, and Belton Evans and Oliver Jackson on drums. Rudy Van Gelder recorded the album.

The album has six long tracks of a little over five to a little over seven minutes. King Curtis wrote the title track Soul Meeting, Lazy Soul and Do You Have Soul Now? himself. In addition, the band plays Jeep's Blues by Duke Ellington and Johnny Hodges, the ballad All the Way and Cole Porter's What Is This Thing Called Love. The long tracks give the soloists all the space they need.
werk/king-curtis-soul-meeting.listen: Listen to Soul Meeting and notice how saxophone and trumpet take turns leading above the rhythm section.

werk/kings-of-leon-aha-shake-heartbreak.text:
The second studio album by Kings of Leon was released in Europe in November 2004 and in the United States in February 2005, with a different cover. As with its predecessor, the producer Ethan Johns was behind the controls, at his Three Crows Studio in Los Angeles. It housed the old mixing desk from Abbey Road, on which the Beatles had also worked.

The title comes from the third song, Taper Jean Girl. Because of coarse language in that song, among others, as well as Rememo, Soft and Four Kicks, it is the band's only album with a Parental Advisory. The British version shows a white orchid on a black background and includes the bonus track Where Nobody Knows. The Bucket, Four Kicks and King of the Rodeo were released as singles. The reviews were generally favourable, and Rolling Stone later placed the album at number 39 among the best records of the 2000s.
werk/kings-of-leon-aha-shake-heartbreak.listen: Listen to Four Kicks and notice how the band keeps the tempo and energy high, with guitar, bass and drums thundering ahead together.

werk/kings-of-leon-because-of-the-times.text:
Because of the Times is the third studio album by Kings of Leon and was released on 2 April 2007 in the United Kingdom, a day later in the United States. It received positive reviews overall and appeared on many album-of-the-year lists.

Opinions differed. NME wrote that the album made the band one of the great American groups of the day, and Entertainment Weekly called it a widescreen movie on CD. Others felt that the four Followill brothers and cousins were experimenting and losing their way a little. NME placed it at number 6 among the best albums of the year and Rolling Stone at number 31. In 2009 Clash placed it at number 3 on a list of the most important albums since 2004.
werk/kings-of-leon-because-of-the-times.listen: Listen to Knocked Up, the opening track, and notice the vocals and the guitars.

werk/kings-of-leon-come-around-sundown.text:
Come Around Sundown is the fifth studio album by Kings of Leon. It was released in mid-October 2010 by RCA, first in Ireland, Austria and Germany, a few days later in the United Kingdom and North America. The first single, Radioactive, premiered with a video on the band's website on 8 September.

Jacquire King and Angelo Petraglia produced the album, and the line-up is broad: besides the Followill brothers, saxophone, fiddle, sitar, theremin and trumpet are among the instruments heard. The album went straight to number one in several countries and reached number two in the United States. It was nominated for a Grammy for Best Rock Album. The critics were positive overall. Rolling Stone placed it at number 18 among the best albums of 2010 and Q at number 25.
werk/kings-of-leon-come-around-sundown.listen: Listen to Radioactive, the first single, and notice how voice and instruments together form the sound of the band.

werk/kings-of-leon-only-by-the-night.text:
Only by the Night is the fourth studio album by Kings of Leon, released in September 2008. The writing began only a few days after the previous record, Because of the Times, came out. The producers Jacquire King and Angelo Petraglia recorded it at Blackbird Studio in Nashville. The main parts of each track were put down live on 16-track analogue tape and later worked on further in Pro Tools.

The singles became big hits. Sex on Fire reached number one in the United Kingdom and Australia, among other countries, and Use Somebody was the band's first top 10 hit in the United States. The opening track Closer stands out for a three-note bass riff, with an octave effect from an effects pedal. The critical response was divided: American sites gave low scores, while British magazines were enthusiastic. Use Somebody later won a Grammy for Record of the Year, and Q named the album the best of 2008.
werk/kings-of-leon-only-by-the-night.listen: Listen to Closer and notice the three-note bass riff with its floating effect: what does it do to the mood of the opening track?

werk/kings-of-leon-sex-on-fire.text: Sex on Fire by Kings of Leon, three brothers and a cousin from the Followill family, was released in September 2008. They grew up in the American South and began with southern rock, in the line of Lynyrd Skynyrd. Sex on Fire, from the album Only by the Night, became their first number one, in England, Ireland, Australia and Finland. After that, rock was less and less often found at the top of the charts.
werk/kings-of-leon-sex-on-fire.listen: Hear the raw voice of Caleb Followill and the ringing guitar figure that carries on through the whole song.

werk/kings-of-leon-youth-en-young-manhoo.text:
With this debut from 2003, Kings of Leon introduced themselves to a wider audience. The album was released in July 2003 in the United Kingdom and in August in the United States. It was recorded in three studios: Shangri-La in Malibu, Sound City in Van Nuys and Ocean Way in Nashville.

The music is southern rock with influences from punk and garage rock. Molly's Chambers, Wasted Time and California Waiting were released as singles. Red Morning Light was a promotional single and turned up in a commercial for the Ford Focus and in the game FIFA 2004. Holy Roller Novocaine later ended up in a film. The critics responded generally positively: NME counted the album among the best debuts of the decade and The Village Voice called it the best rock debut of 2003. In the United Kingdom it reached number 3. In the United States it did not make the top hundred.
werk/kings-of-leon-youth-en-young-manhoo.listen: Listen to Red Morning Light and notice how raw the guitars and the vocals sound.

werk/kiss-destroyer.text:
Destroyer is the fourth studio album by Kiss and was released on 15 March 1976 by Casablanca Records. After the breakthrough with the live album Alive!, Bob Ezrin, known for his work with Alice Cooper, became the producer. He rejected most of the demo material. Only heavily reworked versions of God of Thunder and Detroit Rock City made it onto the record. Ezrin even gave the members a lesson in basic music theory and wore a whistle during the recording. Paul Stanley called it a musical boot camp.

The sound gained more layers than on the first three records. Ezrin added sound effects, strings, screaming children and a children's choir, and in God of Thunder reversed drums can be heard. Great Expectations uses the beginning of a theme from Beethoven's Sonate Pathétique. Detroit Rock City tells of a fan who died in a car accident on the way to a concert. Destroyer was the band's first album to go platinum.
werk/kiss-destroyer.listen: Listen to God of Thunder and notice the reversed drums, one of the effects that Ezrin devised in the studio.

werk/kiss-dressed-to-kill.text:
Dressed to Kill is the third studio album by Kiss and was released on 19 March 1975. The financial worries of the label Casablanca did not allow for a professional producer, so label boss Neil Bogart and the band produced it themselves. The recording took ten days in February 1975, in Studio B of Electric Lady. Gene Simmons said that Ladies in Waiting was written in a single afternoon in the studio and quickly taught to the band.

At a little over thirty minutes, it is the band's shortest studio record. On the cover the band members wear suits, although only Peter Criss owned one himself. Rock and Roll All Nite, Rock Bottom, C'mon and Love Me and She remained staples of the concerts. The album reached number 32 in the American chart and went gold in 1977. The live version of Rock and Roll All Nite later that year reached number 12 as a single.
werk/kiss-dressed-to-kill.listen: Listen to Rock and Roll All Nite and notice the chorus, in which the roadies sing too.

werk/kiss-hotter-than-hell.text:
For their second album, the four New Yorkers went to Los Angeles in 1974, where the producers Kenny Kerner and Richie Wise had just moved. It was the first time the band had recorded outside their home state, and they did not feel at home there. On the first day, Paul Stanley's guitar was stolen. The album sounds darker than the debut, because of the muddy production and the lyrics. Goin' Blind is about a doomed love between a man of 93 and a girl of 16, and Watchin' You about a stalking voyeur. Ace Frehley co-wrote but did not yet dare to sing. His solo in Strange Ways is considered one of his best.

The album did far worse than the debut. There was no hit, and the only single was released in small numbers. Even so, Parasite, Hotter Than Hell and Watchin' You remained staples on stage.
werk/kiss-hotter-than-hell.listen: Listen to Parasite and notice the rough, direct sound: can you hear that the production here is dark rather than polished?

werk/kiss-kiss.text:
The debut by Kiss was released on 8 February 1974 by Casablanca Records. Gene Simmons and Paul Stanley had already written many of the songs for their previous band Wicked Lester. The recording took place at Bell Sound Studios in New York and, according to the producer Richie Wise, lasted only thirteen days. The music is solid, direct rock, with Strutter as the opener, kicked off by a drum intro. Cold Gin was the first song that Ace Frehley wrote for the band; because he did not dare to sing, Simmons took over the vocals. Nothin' to Lose became the first single. Kissin' Time was not on the first pressing and was recorded two months later, when it became clear that the record was not achieving the hoped-for success.

At the presentation the show became so bombastic that Warner Bros. threatened to end the collaboration unless the face paint disappeared. The band refused.
werk/kiss-kiss.listen: Listen to Strutter and notice how the song opens with a drum intro: can you hear how the band then launches straight into full swing?

werk/kitaro-kojiki.text:
Kojiki is an album by the new age musician Kitaro from 1990. It is based on the Kojiki, a classic Japanese book of ancient history and legends. The record received a Grammy nomination in 1990.

The sound combines his characteristic keyboards and flute sounds with the string orchestra of the Skywalker Symphony. The seven tracks bear Japanese titles, such as Hajimari, Orochi and Matsuri. Matsuri later left traces in the 1997 Bollywood film Gupt: according to the article about the record, the flute music and the prelude of one of its songs were partly influenced by this piece.
werk/kitaro-kojiki.listen: Listen in Matsuri to the flute and the keyboards. Notice how the strings add colour to them.

werk/kitaro-the-light-of-the-spirit.text:
The Light of the Spirit was released in 1987 and is a studio album by Kitaro. He produced it together with Mickey Hart, the drummer of the Grateful Dead. Many guests play on it, including Zakir Hussain on percussion, David Grisman on mandolin and Bobby Black on pedal steel guitar.

The album combines synthesizers with acoustic instruments. The magazine CD Review called it a lush wave of synthesizer orchestrations with acoustic colours. The track The Field earned a Grammy nomination. The record consists of eight tracks, with Sundance, Moondance and Howling Thunder alongside the title track.
werk/kitaro-the-light-of-the-spirit.listen: Listen in The Field to how synthesizer sounds and acoustic colours intermingle.

werk/klaus-schulze-audentity.text:
Audentity is Klaus Schulze's fifteenth album and was released in 1983. Like its predecessor Trancefer, it leans heavily on sequencers, but the style is less harsh, especially in Cellistica and Spielglocken. Besides the composer, Rainer Bloss (sounds and glockenspiel), Michael Shrieve (EEH computer and Simmons percussion) and Wolfgang Tiepold (cello) take part.

Not every track revolves around sequencers. Sebastian im Traum, named after a collection of poems by Georg Trakl, points ahead to the operatic style of later works such as Totentag. A short sequencer phrase from this track can be heard in Michael Mann's 1986 film Manhunter. In 2005 the album was reissued by Revisited Records, with a different track order.
werk/klaus-schulze-audentity.listen: Listen to Cellistica and notice the sequencers, which sound less harsh here, and the cello, which adds a human sound to them.

werk/klaus-schulze-dig-it.text:
Dig It is Klaus Schulze's thirteenth album and was released in 1980. It is his first fully digital recording. The composer plays synthesizer, guitar, drums and keyboards, works with computers and also sings. Fred Severloh also plays drums. In 2005 Revisited Records reissued the album, the sixth of his that this label reissued. That edition includes a bonus DVD with the performance at Ars Electronica in 1980, which had previously appeared as audio on The Ultimate Edition from 2000.

The opening track Death of an Analogue later became the main theme of the Australian horror film Next of Kin from 1982, starring Jacki Kerin and John Jarratt.
werk/klaus-schulze-dig-it.listen: Listen to Death of an Analogue, the track that later became the main music of a horror film, and notice the atmosphere the synthesizers create.

werk/klein-orkest-over-de-muur.text: In 1984 Over de muur by Klein Orkest became a hit. The singer and lyricist Harrie Jekkers came from cabaret. The song is about East and West Berlin and asks whether life in the West is really so much freer than in the East. That was not an obvious question at the time. Five years later the Wall fell. Here kleinkunst (Dutch cabaret song) and pop come together: a narrative song with a chorus that everyone sings along to.
werk/klein-orkest-over-de-muur.listen: Hear how Jekkers tells the story, with a comparison between East and West, and a chorus to sing along to.

werk/kool-en-the-gang-spirit-of-the-boog.text:
Spirit of the Boogie is the sixth studio album by Kool & the Gang and was released in 1975. It is a follow-up to Wild and Peaceful from 1973. The instrumental Jungle Jazz uses the same basic rhythm as Jungle Boogie, but lets the players improvise on saxophone, trumpet and flute. There are also references to earlier work: Ancestral Ceremony contains the line making merry music, the name of a song on the 1972 album Good Times. Donald Boyce, who rapped in Jungle Boogie, can be heard again on the title track. There are African influences, and in Caribbean Festival the band plays in a West Indian style, again with plenty of room for improvisation.

The drum rhythm after the fill at the start of Jungle Jazz has been sampled in more than fifty songs, including Pump Up the Volume by M/A/R/R/S.
werk/kool-en-the-gang-spirit-of-the-boog.listen: Listen in Jungle Jazz to the drum rhythm directly after the fill at the start, which has been sampled in more than fifty songs.

werk/kool-en-the-gang-wild-and-peaceful.text:
Wild and Peaceful is the fourth studio album by the funk band Kool & the Gang and marked their commercial breakthrough. The group produced and arranged the record themselves and recorded it at Mediasound Studios in New York. The album yielded the band's first three Top 10 singles: Funky Stuff, Jungle Boogie and Hollywood Swinging. The magazine Record World praised Funky Stuff as funk and fun, with plenty of percussion and whistles.

The album was released in 1973 and reached number 6 on the Billboard R&B chart, where it stayed for 36 weeks. It was also the group's first album in the Top 40 of the pop chart, at number 33. Jungle Boogie and Hollywood Swinging each sold more than a million copies, and the record itself was certified gold.
werk/kool-en-the-gang-wild-and-peaceful.listen: Listen to Funky Stuff and notice the percussion and the whistles that make the song so cheerful.

werk/korn-follow-the-leader.text:
For the third album, the band chose a producer other than Ross Robinson for the first time: Steve Thompson, together with the engineer Toby Wright. Halfway through the recording, Thompson was fired, after which Wright took over and all the vocal tracks had to be recorded again. Robinson stayed on as a vocal coach. Guests include Ice Cube on Children of the Korn and Fred Durst on All In the Family. The cover, drawn by the team of Todd McFarlane, shows a child skipping towards the edge of a cliff.

Critics heard metal with industrial touches and hip hop rhythms. It's On opens with distorted guitars, heavy beats and a scream of rage. Got the Life and Freak On a Leash became singles, and the video for Freak On a Leash won awards. The reviews were largely positive. The album is regarded as the record that brought nu metal into the mainstream.
werk/korn-follow-the-leader.listen: Listen to the distorted guitars and the beats in It's On, and notice how the singer screams out his anger.

werk/korn-issues.text:
Issues is the fourth studio album by the American nu metal band Korn. It was released on 16 November 1999 by Immortal and Epic Records, with Brendan O'Brien as producer. The drummer David Silveria described the new music as simpler and heavier, with grooves more like those of the early years, and said that the singer Jonathan Davis had become a much better singer. In October 1999 the band put Falling Away from Me on their own website as a free MP3, against the advice of their lawyers. For every fan who signed up, the group donated money to two children's charities, which raised more than 250,000 dollars.

The cover was a fan design, chosen through an MTV contest. The album reached number 1 on the Billboard 200. To mark the release, the band played the entire album in order at the Apollo Theater in Harlem, where soul and R&B were normally the sound. The reviews were mixed.
werk/korn-issues.listen: Listen to Falling Away from Me and notice the heavy grooves and Davis's vocals. What does the voice do to the music beneath it?

werk/korn-korn.text:
Korn recorded their debut in May and June 1994 at Indigo Ranch Studios in Malibu, with the producer Ross Robinson, who had also made their 1993 demo. The group played most of the record live together, rather than instrument by instrument. The studio stood on a hill, so recording could also be done outside. Immortal/Epic had signed the band after a performance in Huntington Beach, because they were unwilling to give up creative freedom.

For many, the album counts as the first nu metal album: the heavy sounds of extreme metal combined with vocals, clothing and rhythms from hip hop. Blind opens with the two guitars of James Shaffer and Brian Welch and the opening line Are you ready?. The lyrics deal with child abuse, drug use and bullying. Faget is about the school years of the singer Jonathan Davis, who was bullied. The album reached number 72 on the Billboard 200 and by 2003 had already sold 2.1 million copies in the United States.
werk/korn-korn.listen: Listen to Shoots and Ladders and notice the bagpipes: the singer walked outside past the studio playing them, which is why the sound naturally becomes softer.

werk/korn-life-is-peachy.text:
After fourteen months of touring with the debut, Korn took a month off and began work on a second album. The group returned to the producer Ross Robinson and to Indigo Ranch Studios in Malibu, where the first album had also been recorded. Most of it came together in the studio itself, quickly, to preserve the energy of the stage. The guitarists wanted more melody and atmosphere and used volume swells and effects pedals, while the bassist crossed hip hop beats with his bass lines. The singer Jonathan Davis wrote lyrics about drugs, sex, betrayal and revenge.

The album includes No Place to Hide, A.D.I.D.A.S. and Good God, among others. The vocals in Good God were seen as the heart of the record. Critics were divided, but praised the writing and the sound: metal with hip hop beats. The album became the band's first major breakthrough and contributed to what would later be called nu metal.
werk/korn-life-is-peachy.listen: Listen to Jonathan Davis's vocals in Good God and notice how much emotion he puts into his voice.

werk/korn-untouchables.text:
Untouchables is the fifth studio album by the American nu metal band Korn and was released on 11 June 2002. The group began writing in early 2001. Tension between the members was rising, and so they worked for a time in Scottsdale, Arizona. Recording took place in Hollywood and Los Angeles, with Michael Beinhorn as producer and Andy Wallace as mixer. It was the first album recorded in 96 kHz digital sound. Because of the lengthy work, it cost about three million dollars. The drums alone took a month, with fifty microphones on the kit, and Jonathan Davis's vocals took months.

Here to Stay, the first single, won a Grammy. The album entered at number two on the Billboard 200 behind The Eminem Show. Davis blames the disappointing sales on piracy, because the album leaked months earlier. The reviews were favourable, and in 2021 Metal Hammer named it the group's best album.
werk/korn-untouchables.listen: Listen to Here to Stay and notice the interplay of guitars, bass, drums and Davis's vocals. Which sound comes to the fore?

werk/kraftwerk-autobahn.text:
Florian Schneider and Ralf Hütter were a duo when they made Autobahn, but they had help from Klaus Röder on guitar and violin and from Wolfgang Flür on percussion. The album came about partly in their own Kling Klang studio, but mostly in Conny Plank's new studio near Cologne. They bought a Minimoog and used modified rhythm machines. Emil Schult, who studied with Joseph Beuys, helped with lyrics and with a new look for the group.

Most of the record is the twenty-two-minute title track, inspired by the pleasure of driving along the German motorway, with sounds that imitate a journey. With it, Kraftwerk made the transition from experimental krautrock to electropop. In Germany the album received little attention, but an American radio station in Chicago played the track as a single, after which it spread and became an international hit in 1975. The first reviews were mixed, later there was much praise, and David Bowie cited it as an influence.
werk/kraftwerk-autobahn.listen: Listen in Autobahn to the sounds that imitate a car journey, and notice how the simple melody keeps returning.

werk/kronos-quartet-pieces-of-africa.text:
In 1992 Pieces of Africa was released, an album of works that the Kronos Quartet had commissioned from seven African composers. The four string players play violin, viola and cello, and also play the akete. In addition, guest musicians are heard on kora, mbira, tar, oud and bendir, among other instruments, and the Oakland Interfaith Gospel Choir sings along. Judith Sherman produced the album.

AllMusic wrote that the quartet avoids cultural appropriation and that the album is full of charming melodies, making it one of the group's most accessible and best projects. Gramophone considered only Escalay and White Man Sleeps successful compositions for string quartet. In 2024 the Library of Congress added the album to the National Recording Registry, because it is culturally, historically or aesthetically significant.
werk/kronos-quartet-pieces-of-africa.listen: Listen in Escalay, one of the two pieces that Gramophone found successful, to how four string players together carry a single composition.

werk/kronos-quartet-winter-was-hard.text:
Winter Was Hard presents the Kronos Quartet with a wide choice of music: pieces by Aulis Sallinen, Terry Riley, Arvo Pärt, Anton Webern, John Zorn, John Lurie, Astor Piazzolla, Alfred Schnittke and Samuel Barber. The quartet consists of David Harrington, John Sherba, Hank Dutt and Joan Jeanrenaud. Most of the recordings date from November 1987 in Methuen, Massachusetts. The title piece was recorded in January 1988 in a church in San Francisco, with the San Francisco Girls Chorus and a harmonium.

Forbidden Fruit was produced by Zorn, with turntables by Christian Marclay and the voice of Ohta Hiromi. The album placed 11th in the Los Angeles Times Classical Top 25 of 1989. Brian Olewnick calls it a typical early mixture of contemporary music with a downtown edge and twentieth-century classics.
werk/kronos-quartet-winter-was-hard.listen: Listen in Forbidden Fruit to the turntables of Christian Marclay and the voice of Ohta Hiromi: how does that sound on an album of string quartet music?

werk/kylie-minogue-enjoy-yourself.text:
After the success of her debut, Kylie Minogue went back to work in London in February 1989 with the producers Stock Aitken Waterman, who wrote and produced nine of the ten tracks. The recording ran until July and coincided with the filming of The Delinquents, her first feature film. The album sounds like bubblegum pop, dance-pop and disco and is mostly about romantic relationships. The makers wanted more variety than on the previous record, with R&B bass lines, among other things, and a song in the style of a 1950s orchestra. Tell Tale Signs is a jazzy love song full of strings, and My Secret Heart has peculiar rhythms and stuttering cello. Tears on My Pillow is a cover of a song from 1958.

The critical response was mixed, mainly because the album resembled the debut so closely. Hand on Your Heart and Tears on My Pillow reached number one in the United Kingdom.
werk/kylie-minogue-enjoy-yourself.listen: Listen to My Secret Heart and notice the unusual rhythms, the key changes and the stuttering cello sound. How far is this from ordinary dance music?

werk/kylie-minogue-i-should-be-so-lucky.text: Kylie Minogue was known in Australia as an actress in the soap Neighbours. When she came to London in 1987, it turned out that Stock Aitken Waterman had forgotten she was coming. There was no song ready. According to the story, Stock and Aitken wrote I Should Be So Lucky in about forty minutes while she waited outside. In February 1988 it was number one in England.
werk/kylie-minogue-i-should-be-so-lucky.listen: The song is about someone who is only lucky in love in her dreams. Hear how the chorus sticks in your head right away.

werk/kylie-minogue-let-s-get-to-it.text:
Let's Get to It is Kylie Minogue's fourth studio album and her last with Pete Waterman Limited. It was released in October 1991 in the United Kingdom. After Matt Aitken had left Stock Aitken Waterman, Mike Stock and Pete Waterman still wanted to make a record with her. For the first time they shared their writing credits with her, on six tracks. They worked for months at PWL Studios in London, longer than on her earlier albums.

The sound is varied: hip hop, new jack swing, house and dance-pop. Word Is Out opens as new jack swing, and Give Me Just a Little More Time is a cover of Chairmen of the Board. If You Were with Me Now is a duet with Keith Washington, her first duet on an album. Finer Feelings is deliberately more sexual. The reviews were mixed and the album was one of her least successful: it did not make the top ten. Minogue was disappointed and left PWL in 1992.
werk/kylie-minogue-let-s-get-to-it.listen: Listen to Finer Feelings and notice the line in the chorus that refers to Marvin Gaye and Sexual Healing.

werk/lady-gaga-artpop.text:
Lady Gaga began this third album in 2011, shortly after Born This Way. She worked on it during the Born This Way Ball and during her recovery from hip surgery in 2013. She collaborated with, among others, DJ White Shadow, Zedd and Madeon, and the artist Jeff Koons joined the project in 2013. Where Born This Way, in her view, had shown maturity, this album was meant to be more playful and freer.

The album sounds like EDM and synth-pop, with influences from R&B, techno, industrial and dubstep. The lyrics deal with fame, sex and self-determination, with references to Greek and Roman mythology. She wanted the album to sound like a night at the club, with tracks that flow into one another. The first single, Applause, was a success. The reviews were mixed, but later many critics took a more positive view.
werk/lady-gaga-artpop.listen: Listen in Applause to the danceable electronic foundation, and notice how the vocals engage with the theme of audience and fame.

werk/lady-gaga-born-this-way.text:
After The Fame in 2008 and The Fame Monster in 2009, Lady Gaga worked on a third step in her career. She wrote and recorded the album during the Monster Ball Tour, partly on tour buses and in studios from London to Sydney. Fernando Garibay and RedOne helped as producers, and Brian May of Queen and the saxophonist Clarence Clemons of the E Street Band played on it. The producer RedOne called it her freedom album.

Born This Way builds on synth-pop and dance, but adds rock, heavy metal, disco and house. The lyrics deal with sexuality, religion, freedom, feminism and individuality. Religious and conservative commentators were divided, but most critics were positive about the musical variety and the vocals. The title song spent six weeks at number one in the United States. In 2020 Rolling Stone included the record in its list of the five hundred best albums.
werk/lady-gaga-born-this-way.listen: Listen in Judas to the styles that run into one another, and notice how the danceable rhythm and the dark atmosphere together build the tension.

werk/lady-gaga-chromatica.text:
Chromatica is Lady Gaga's fifth solo album, released on 29 May 2020. After the subdued records Joanne and A Star Is Born, she returned to dance music, inspired by early 1990s house. She recorded most of it with BloodPop in her own studio in the Hollywood Hills and at Henson Recording Studios. The record is a concept album about happiness and healing, with lyrics about failed loves and mental struggles. Morgan Kibby wrote three orchestral interludes, recorded with a 26-piece orchestra.

Ariana Grande sings on Rain on Me, Blackpink on Sour Candy and Elton John on Sine from Above. Rain on Me became her fifth number one on the American Hot 100, and the album reached the top of the Billboard 200. Critics praised the craftsmanship and the approach to the subject, although some liked the house sounds less.
werk/lady-gaga-chromatica.listen: Listen to Rain on Me and notice the interplay of the two voices in this duet.

werk/lady-gaga-joanne.text:
Joanne is Lady Gaga's fourth solo album, released on 21 October 2016. After the mixed reception of Artpop and the jazz duets with Tony Bennett, she chose a more subdued sound: dance-pop, soft rock and Americana with country influences, with an emphasis on her voice. Mark Ronson, BloodPop and she herself produced. With Ronson she worked for six months at Rick Rubin's Shangri-La studio in Malibu, and on the first day they wrote Joanne. The song is named after her aunt Joanne Germanotta, whose death strongly influenced the record.

Josh Homme plays guitar on John Wayne, Beck collaborated on Dancin' in Circles and Florence Welch sings on Hey Girl. Perfect Illusion, Million Reasons and Joanne were released as singles. The critical response was largely favourable, although some found the album lacking in cohesion. The title song won a Grammy.
werk/lady-gaga-joanne.listen: Listen to Hey Girl and notice how the two singers alternate and sing together in this duet.

werk/ladysmith-black-mambazo-amabutho.text:
Amabutho is the first album by Ladysmith Black Mambazo, the South African group that sings isicathamiya. It was released in 1973 by the Gallo Record Company. Seven men sing on the record, including Joseph Shabalala, Milton Mazibuko and Albert Mazibuko.

The album contains the hit Nomathemba. Amabutho became the first record by Black musicians in South Africa to receive a gold disc, for 25,000 copies sold. In 2007 Gallo reissued the record, in South Africa only, together with most of the group's early work. The titles are Zulu: Amabutho means warriors and Nomathemba means hope.
werk/ladysmith-black-mambazo-amabutho.listen: Listen to Nomathemba and notice how the voices of the seven men together form a whole.

werk/ladytron-604.text:
604 is the debut album by the English electronic band Ladytron. It was released on 6 February 2001 in the United States by Emperor Norton and on 12 March in the United Kingdom by Invicta Hi-Fi. Lance Thomas co-produced the album, recorded it and mixed it. Some of the tracks had already appeared on earlier EPs: Miss Black and Her Friends, Mu-Tron EP and Commodore Rock. The title refers to the area code of the region around Vancouver in British Columbia.

The first single was He Took Her to a Movie, recorded for fifty pounds and featuring guest vocals by Lisa Eriksson. The song was inspired by The Model by Kraftwerk, and NME chose it as single of the week. Critics responded generally with praise, and the magazine Muzik made the record album of the month in March 2001.
werk/ladytron-604.listen: Listen in He Took Her to a Movie to Lisa Eriksson's vocals and compare the atmosphere with The Model by Kraftwerk.

werk/ladytron-light-en-magic.text:
Light & Magic is the second studio album by the English band Ladytron. It was released on 17 September 2002 in the United States by Emperor Norton and on 2 December in the United Kingdom by Telstar Records. An earlier version of NuHorizons had already appeared as a B-side on the 2001 single The Way That I Found You, under the title Holiday 601. Seventeen appeared on the soundtrack of the 2003 film Party Monster, and the instrumental version was used in television commercials for a Christina Aguilera perfume.

The press was enthusiastic. Rolling Stone included the album on its list of the fifty best albums of 2002, Muzik called it the best electropop of that year and Drowned in Sound placed it at number 14 on its year-end list. NME placed it at number 41.
werk/ladytron-light-en-magic.listen: Listen in Seventeen to the melody and consider whether it stands up without vocals, as in the commercial.

werk/lalo-schifrin-piano-espanol.text:
Piano Español is an album by the Argentine pianist, composer and conductor Lalo Schifrin. It was recorded in New York in 1959 and released on the Tico label. In 1968 it was reissued by Roulette under the title Lalolé: The Latin Sound of Lalo Schifrin.

Schifrin plays piano and made the arrangements. He conducts an orchestra with, among others, trumpets, saxophones, bass clarinet, oboe, bongos, harp and strings. The repertoire ranges from Latin American and Spanish pieces such as Frenesi, Malagueña and El Cumbanchero to Caravan and All the Things You Are. He wrote Hullabalues himself together with Ralph Seijo.
werk/lalo-schifrin-piano-espanol.listen: Listen to Malagueña and notice how the piano holds on to the Spanish character of the piece.

werk/lamont-dozier-out-here-on-my-own.text:
Out Here on My Own is the debut album by Lamont Dozier, released by ABC. McKinley Jackson produced the record. Gene Page, H.B. Barnum and Paul Riser wrote the arrangements, and the studio line-up included Ray Parker Jr. on bass and guitar, the guitarists Wah Wah Watson and David T. Walker, the percussionist King Errisson and a large group of string and wind players.

According to Ron Wynn of AllMusic, the album is among the better combinations of social commentary and urgent soul singing of its day. The singles became hits. Trying To Hold On To My Woman reached number 4 on the American R&B chart and number 15 on the pop chart in 1974. Fish Ain't Bitin' reached number 26 on the Hot 100 and likewise number 4 on the R&B chart.
werk/lamont-dozier-out-here-on-my-own.listen: Listen in Out Here On My Own to the urgent soul singing and try to hear what the lyrics are about.

werk/lange-frans-en-baas-b-zinloos.text: On 5 October 2004 Zinloos by Lange Frans & Baas B was released, with the singer Ninthe on the chorus. The song protests against zinloos geweld (senseless violence), violence without any provocation, and names victims such as Meindert Tjoelker. It spent three weeks at number 1 in the Top 40. In this way Nederhop (Dutch hip hop) showed that rap could also deal with social subjects that touched the whole of the Netherlands.
werk/lange-frans-en-baas-b-zinloos.listen: Hear the contrast between the narrative raps in the verses and Ninthe's sung, sorrowful chorus.

werk/larry-carlton-sleepwalk.text:
Sleepwalk is the fifth studio album by the guitarist Larry Carlton and was released on 6 January 1982. He produced, engineered and mixed the record himself. He wrote the string arrangements and conducted them, while Al Schmitt recorded the strings. The album was mastered by Mike Reese at The Mastering Lab in Hollywood.

The line-up is large and versatile. Abe Laboriel plays bass, and Steve Gadd and Jeff Porcaro share the drumming between them, while John Ferraro drums on one track. Paulinho da Costa plays percussion and David Sanborn plays saxophone on one track. Terry Trotter, Brian Mann, Don Freeman and Greg Mathieson share the keyboards between them.
werk/larry-carlton-sleepwalk.listen: Listen to Upper Kern and notice David Sanborn's saxophone alongside the guitar.

werk/larry-carlton-strikes-twice.text:
Strikes Twice is the fourth studio album by the guitarist Larry Carlton and was released in August 1980. He produced and arranged the record himself and also handled the engineering. Jay Graydon advised on the remix. The album was mastered by Bernie Grundman at A&M Studios in Hollywood.

You hear the leader himself on guitar and, on three tracks, also on guitar synthesizer, and he sings on three tracks. Greg Mathieson, Don Freeman and Brian Mann play keyboards, Pops Popwell plays bass, John Ferraro drums and Paulinho da Costa plays percussion. On the final track, For Love Alone, he also plays Fender Rhodes, bass, drums and percussion himself.
werk/larry-carlton-strikes-twice.listen: Listen to For Love Alone and try to hear how many different instruments one man plays on this track.

werk/larry-young-groove-street.text:
Groove Street was recorded in 1962 and released on the Prestige label. It is an album by the jazz organist Larry Young, who here plays in a quartet with the tenor saxophonist Bill Leslie, the guitarist Thornel Schwartz and the drummer Jimmie Smith. The record has five tracks. Two of them are standards by other composers, I Found a New Baby and Sweet Lorraine. Young wrote the rest himself, including the title track and the longest piece, Gettin' into It, which lasts more than fourteen minutes.

AllMusic gave the album three stars. According to that review, nothing of real substance happens, but fans of Jimmy Smith will enjoy the similar style that Young had at that time.
werk/larry-young-groove-street.listen: Listen to Gettin' into It, at over fourteen minutes the longest track, and notice how the organ, the tenor saxophone and the guitar take turns in the spotlight.

werk/larry-young-into-somethin.text:
Into Somethin' from 1965 was the debut of the jazz organist Larry Young on the Blue Note label. He plays in a quartet with the tenor saxophonist Sam Rivers, the guitarist Grant Green and the drummer Elvin Jones. He had already recorded with Green and Jones, on records under the guitarist's name, so the collaboration was not new.

The album contains five tracks, almost all by Young himself. Plaza De Toros is the exception: Green wrote that one. The longest pieces, Tyrone and Plaza De Toros, both last almost ten minutes, so there is ample time for soloing. Sam Rivers is heard on the first four tracks, but not on Ritha. The 1998 CD reissue adds an alternative version of Ritha.
werk/larry-young-into-somethin.listen: Listen to Plaza De Toros, the only track that Grant Green wrote himself, and notice how organ, guitar and Elvin Jones's drums follow one another in the long solos.

werk/larry-young-testifying.text:
Testifying is the debut album by the jazz organist Larry Young and was recorded in 1960. It was released on the New Jazz label. Besides the organ, we hear Joe Holiday on tenor saxophone, Thornel Schwartz on guitar and Jimmie Smith on drums.

The programme consists of seven tracks. The organist wrote the title composition himself. The other pieces are the work of others, including Rodgers and Hart, Hammerstein and Romberg, J.J. Johnson and Joe Holiday. Standards such as Falling in Love With Love stand alongside jazz pieces such as Wee Dot. AllMusic gave the album three stars and found it easy to recommend to lovers of jazz organ.
werk/larry-young-testifying.listen: Listen to the title track Testifying and notice the role of the organ alongside the guitar and saxophone sound.

werk/laurie-anderson-mister-heartbreak.text:
Mister Heartbreak is the second studio album by Laurie Anderson, released on 14 February 1984 by Warner Bros. Records. She wanted to make a record that could exist without images, and used the Synclavier on every track. Besides the distorted voice of her first album, she also sings normally here. The guitarist Adrian Belew of King Crimson played on four tracks; in Sharkey's Day he opted for an aggressive sound with a fuzz pedal. Peter Gabriel co-wrote and sang on Excellent Birds, and William S. Burroughs spoke the text of Sharkey's Night. Gravity's Angel borrows imagery from the novel Gravity's Rainbow by Thomas Pynchon.

Billboard called it an intriguing collection of songs that uncompromisingly links new music and the avant-garde.
werk/laurie-anderson-mister-heartbreak.listen: Listen in Sharkey's Day to Adrian Belew's guitar: can you hear the aggressive sound of his fuzz pedal?

werk/lauryn-hill-the-miseducation-of-lau.text:
After the break-up of the Fugees, Lauryn Hill made her first solo album in 1998. She was pregnant with her first child and wrote more than thirty songs in her attic studio in New Jersey. The recording ran from September 1997 to June 1998, first in New York and New Jersey, then at Tuff Gong Studios in Kingston, Bob Marley's studio. She wrote and produced almost everything herself, with a group of musicians called New Ark.

It is a concept album about learning from love, with themes such as relationships, conflict, motherhood and faith. The sound is neo soul and R&B with hip hop and reggae, played with real instruments and layered harmony vocals. Doo Wop (That Thing) became a number one in the United States. The critical response was unanimously glowing, the album won Album of the Year at the Grammys and contributed to the breakthrough of hip hop and neo soul.
werk/lauryn-hill-the-miseducation-of-lau.listen: Listen to Doo Wop (That Thing). Notice the harmonies and the live bass, and hear how she sings and raps in the same song.
